messages:
Mike: Heads-up — we need a large assignable IPv4 block + quota bumps in eu-west-3 to bootstrap the new Dedicated GPU cluster. Target: 50 A100 nodes in the first wave, likely 3 NICs/node, 8 secondary private IPs per NIC, and ~120 public IPs for customer endpoints. Timeline: 2–3 weeks.

Jana: Got it. Can you put exact numbers (ENIs, EIPs, secondary IPs) and a short justification? AWS defaults are tiny for EIP/ENI per account.

Mike: Quick math: 50 nodes * 3 ENIs = 150 ENIs. Each ENI needs 8 secondaries -> 1200 secondary private IPs. Public-facing endpoints ~120 EIPs (some will be NATed), plus headroom for autoscaling and canary -> request EIP quota to 300 and ENI quota to 2000. Also request a VPC secondary CIDR /22 (1024 IPs) and an assignable block so we don't hit fragmentation.

Lisa: Recommend we also request an IPv6 /56 from the account to avoid running out of IPv4 addresses for internal pods. IPv6 would let us avoid >100 EIPs by using global IPv6 addressing + ALB dualstack. Downsides: some customer infra still needs IPv4. :thinking_face:

Aditya: Important: some enterprise customers require static public IPv4 per tenant for routing. We can't move all traffic to IPv6. We should lock at least 120 public IPv4s that are assignable to instances/ENIs.

Mike: Agreed. Plan: (1) request EIP quota bump to 300, (2) ENI quota bump to 2000 in eu-west-3, (3) request VPC secondary /22, (4) request IPv6 /56. I've drafted the support payload below.

Mike: ```
# AWS Service Quotas / Support case payload (draft)
Region: eu-west-3
Quotas:
 - Elastic IPs: increase to 300 (current: 5)
 - Network interfaces (ENI): increase to 2000 (current: 350)
 - VPC secondary IPv4 CIDR: request /22 (1024 addresses)
 - Assign IPv6 /56 to VPC
Justification: Onboarding Dedicated GPU fleet (50 A100 nodes) for EU production. Requires stable public addressing for customer endpoints and headroom for autoscale. Traffic estimates attached.
Attachments: traffic_forecast_q2.pdf, network_diagram.png, security_controls.md
``` 

Jana: Nice. Add expected egress traffic numbers and explain why NAT alone isn't OK (cost + single point of failure unless we scale NAT infra). Also include the list of accounts and org id.

Aditya: Also include SLA requirement: < 30s to reprovision new node with public IP assigned. That helps with quota approvals.

cloud-support-bot: Support case created: case-2026-04567. Status: pending. Reference: case-2026-04567. ETA for first response: 24 hours.

Helga (AWS Support): Hi team — I'm on the case. Quick notes: EIP increases to 300 are usually accepted with justification but can take 3–7 business days. ENI increases depend on instance family caps; we'll coordinate with service team. IPv6 /56 is available in eu-west-3 but must be associated at VPC creation or via modify-vpc-attribute; we'll need VPC IDs. Please attach the architecture diagram and list of affected account IDs. If you want faster provisioning for canary, we can do a temporary EIP pool via our partner account — ask if you want that path.

Tyler: Thanks — can you also note whether we should pre-allocate NAT gateway elastic IPs or spin up per-subnet NAT autoscaled fleet? Cost question: NAT per-hour + per-GB can add up if everything egresses IPv4.

Lisa: For cost: rough numbers — 10 TB/mo egress through NAT gateways vs direct EIPs+ALB will be cheaper where possible. I'll run a quick cost delta and attach.

Mike: Action list from this thread:
- Mike: finalize support payload & attach traffic forecast (today EOD)
- Jana: open formal Service Quotas requests where possible and attach case ref (tomorrow)
- Lisa: cost delta for NAT vs EIP/ALB (48h)
- Aditya: customer list + SLA note (today)

Mike: Ping me for approvals. :+1:

Jana: Closing loop — added case-2026-04567 to our infra board and will update when AWS responds. :wave:
